what: MESH_PLAN step 3 done-test, run live: the 'phone' node signs a grow job addressed to the 'laptop' node and sends it over a real WebRTC DataChannel; the laptop checks it, grows it, seals a v3 answer card and sends it back as a picture; the phone re-runs the answer itself.
honest_scope: Two independent browser nodes on ONE machine (different origins, so separate storage and separate Ed25519 keys). Both keys are now kept non-extractable in IndexedDB, but both were first made by the earlier version of the page as exportable keys in localStorage and moved in on first use — the old copies are deleted, yet a key that was once readable by page script could have been copied before then. A recorded observation, not a regenerable receipt: browser keys and nonces are random. The byte-reproducible receipt for the same protocol is receipts/job-roundtrip.json (CI re-runs it). The two-DEVICE run waits on a second device.

topology.data: both nodes hold data/online_shoppers_intention.csv (data tag b3055ee3)
topology.link: RTCPeerConnection DataChannel, invite + reply pasted by hand (fall-os webrtc.mjs, fall-federate invite check); each node learned the other's key from the invite
topology.stun: none — the STUN box was unticked on both nodes; no third party at all

worker_side: grew it (104 evaluations: 102 for the grow + 2 for the confirmation split) and sent back the signed answer

answer.reason: reproduced 0.820498 here — the signature proves who, the re-run proved what

attacks_on_the_worker.what: the same signed job, sent again
attacks_on_the_worker.reason: this job was already run here — a replay is refused

attacks_on_the_worker.what: the same job with maxEvals changed from 200 to 150, old signature
attacks_on_the_worker.reason: seal mismatch — the requester did not sign this job

attacks_on_the_worker.what: a job validly signed by the same requester but addressed to another worker key (abab…ab)
attacks_on_the_worker.reason: this job is addressed to another worker

network: the phone requested only http://localhost:8150 (page, modules, its data — fetched twice: once by the page, once by a console import used to sign the addressed-elsewhere job) plus one blob: URL (decoding the received answer picture locally); the laptop only http://127.0.0.1:8150. The job and the answer travelled over the DataChannel. Zero requests left the machine.
rule: a worker refuses a job it was not signed, addressed and allowed to run; a requester accepts an answer only if it cites its job, is signed by the worker it chose, and re-runs to the same score on its own machine
